WPSS No. 208 of 2021
With
Stay Application (IA) No.1 of 2021
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel 
for the petitioners.
Notices on behalf of the respondents 
are accepted by Mr. T.S. Phartiyal, learned 
Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the 
State of Uttarakhand. He prays for and is 
granted three weeks’ time to file counter 
affidavit.
By way of an interim measure, it is 
directed that any amount which has 
already been remitted and it has been 
sought to be recovered by the impugned 
order dated 15.12.2020, passed by the 
Chief Education Officer, would not be 
recovered from the salary of the petitioner,
till the next date of listing. 
Respondents may file their counter 
affidavit in three weeks, list thereafter. 
(Sharad Kumar Sharma)

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
WPSS No. 208 of 2021
With connected petitions
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel 
for the petitioners.
2. Mr. Tarun Mohan, learned Brief
Holder for the State.
3. The petitioners are serving as an 
Assistant Teachers in primary institution 
and for certain period they asked for 
medical leave which were forwarded by 
the head master of the institution to the 
Block Education Officer, but no entry was 
made in the service record of the 
petitioners and, thereafter since there was 
no entry of medical leave in the service 
record of the petitioners the recovery was 
ordered which was challenged by the 
petitioners in separate petitions wherein 
on 27.05.2020 and 29.05.2020 the 
recovery was stayed, the copy of which 
are enclosed in the petition. 
4. Thereafter, one person namely
Padam Kumar preferred a writ petition in 
the form of PIL with the following reliefs:-
“(i) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature 
 of mandamus commanding the respondents to 
 conduct and immediate probe or enquiry from 
 any appropriate authority and take necessary 
 action in accordance with law. 
(ii) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature 
of mandamus commanding the respondents to 
conduct the disciplinary proceedings and take 
necessary action against the private 
respondents with regard to the rules and law 
applicable in the instant matter.
(iii) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature 
of mandamus commanding the respondents to 
take affirmative actions of punitive nature 
against the private respondents after assessing 
the conduct of the private respondents.” 5. The Writ Petition (PIL) No. 42 of
2020 was disposed of finally with the 
direction to the respondents to consider 
the representations in accordance with 
law. The representation which was 
directed to be decided are also enclosed as 
Annexure-5 to the petition. Thereafter, by 
the order impugned the Chief Education 
Officer, Haridwar, passed an order dated 
15.12.2020 whereby he revived the earlier 
order of recovery, which, in fact, was 
already stayed by the High Court and 
ordered to recover the amount in six equal 
installments, and it is further mentioned in 
the order that such recovery shall be 
subject to the final outcome of the 
pending petitions. All those pending writ 
petitions are clubbed with this petition. In 
para-9 a specific averment has been made 
that the action of the Chief Education 
Officer while passing the order impugned 
is nothing but a contemptuous act, since, 
in flagrant violation of the interim order 
passed by this Court, the order of recovery 
has been revived. 
6. In this petition, the recovery is 
already stayed and on 27.01.2021, the 
respondents were directed to file counter 
affidavit. It is very strange that up till 
date, the counter affidavit has not been 
filed. 
7. Prima facie, I find force on the
submissions of learned counsel for the 
petitioners that order impugned has been 
passed by the Chief Education Officer, 
Haridwar, in flagrant violation of the 
interim order dated 27.05.2020, passed in 
WPSS No. 507 of 2020 and order dated 
29.05.2020 passed in bunch of petitions 
i.e. WPSS No. 509 of 2020, 510 of 2020, 
511 of 2020, 513 of 2020, 515 of 2020, 
516 of 2020 and 518 of 2020.
8. Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel  for the petitioners apprise to this Court 
that the then Chief Education Officer has 
been re-employed after retirement just 
two months back. If it is so let the said 
officer shall remain present in the Court 
through V.C. to explain why in flagrant
violation of the interim order passed by 
this Court he has passed the order 
impugned.
9. List this case on 06.01.2026.
 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
05.01.2026
Nahid

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS No. 208 of 2021 and other connected petitions
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Sunil Khera, learned Deputy Advocate General 
with Mr. Tarun Mohan, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. Order impugned dated 15.12.2020 has been passed 
apparently in flagrant violation of two interim orders 
passed by this Court on 27.05.2020 and 29.05.2020. It 
appears that by the order impugned dated 15.12.2020, the 
Chief Education Officer has revived the order of recovery, 
which was already stayed by the High Court. Not only this, 
what the Chief Education Officer has done, he directed his 
subordinates to ensure recovery in six instalments and such 
recovery shall be subject to the final outcome of the writ 
petitions, in which recovery was stayed.
4. Yesterday, this matter was listed and after gone 
through the record, this Court was primarily of the view 
that in flagrant violation of the interim orders passed by this 
Court impugned order has been passed. A specific 
averment has been made in the petition that the Chief 
Education Officer in a contemptuous manner passed the 
order impugned. 
5. The then Chief Education Officer Mr. Anand 
Bhardwaj, who is present in person today, submits that 
there is a clerical mistake while dictating the order
impugned.
6. After gone through with the record, this Court is of 
the view that the justification with regard to clerical mistake 
is apparently false and misleading one. 
7. Mr. Bhardwaj further submits that though impugned 
order was passed but no recovery was made. This also 
appears to be a misleading statement since subsequent 
order of recovery was also stayed by this Court. 
8. In such view of the matter, this Court have no option 
except to initiates contempt proceedings against Mr. Anand 
Bhardwaj, the then Chief Education Officer, who may file 
his response by tomorrow. 
9. List on 08.01.2026.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 06.01.2026
SKS

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPSS No. 208 of 2021
With connected petitions
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. Tarun Mohan, learned Brief Holder for the 
State.
3. On 05.01.2026 this court take serious note of the 
fact that the impugned order has been passed by the 
Chief Education Officer, Haridwar, in flagrant violation 
of orders passed on 27.05.2020 and 29.05.2020 passed in 
different petitions, whereby, the recovery was stayed.
4. This court also further take note of one of the PIL 
bearing WPPIL No. 42 of 2020, which was disposed of 
with a direction to the respondents to decide the 
representation of the PIL petitioner.
5. This court also further take note that while 
deciding the representation of PIL petitioner the Chief 
Education Officer while passing the order impugned 
dated 15.12.2020 totally overlooked the interim order 
passed on 27.05.2020 and 29.05.2020 though the 
reference of the order has been given in the order 
impugned.
6. By the order impugned the Chief Education 
Officer passed an order for recovery in six equal 
instalments by observing that such recovery shall be 
subject to the final outcome of the pending petitions in 
which the interim order with regard to recovery of stay 
was passed on 27.05.2020 and 29.05.2020, which are 
clubbed with this petition.
7. In paragraph 19 of this petition a specific 
averment has been made that the action of Chief 
Education Officer, Haridwar while passing the 
impugned order is contemptuous act since the same 
has been passed in flagrant violation of the interim 
orders passed by this court and infact by the order 
impugned the order of recovery was revived.
8. The effect of subsequent order passed by the 
Chief Education Officer dated 15.12.2020 was also  stayed on 27.01.2021 and the counter was called but 
uptill date no counter affidavit has been filed.
9. While taking note of this act of the Chief 
Education Officer that the impugned order has been 
passed in flagrant violation of interim orders the State 
counsel was directed to communicate the then Chief 
Education Officer to be remain present in court to 
explain why in flagrant violation of interim orders the 
impugned order has been passed.
10. In compliance to the order the then Chief 
Education Officer Mr. Anand Bhardwaj present in 
court on 06.01.2026 and make an attempt to justify his 
action by saying that there was a clerical mistake while 
passing the order impugned and furthermore no 
recovery has been made pursuant thereto.
11. This court further take serious note on the 
misleading statement of Mr. Anand Bhardwaj the then 
Chief Education Officer by observing that the 
justification and clarification are misleading one since 
no clerical error apparent on face of the order 
impugned and furthermore the recovery was stayed by 
the High Court.
12. Accordingly, this court was of the view that since 
the order impugned has been passed in flagrant 
violation of the impugned orders and furthermore the 
misleading statement has been given by Mr. Anand 
Bhardwaj the then Chief Education Officer, who was 
asked to file the response.
13. No response has been filed by Mr. Anand 
Bhardwaj and now this court has no option except to 
frame the charge against the then Chief Education 
Officer Mr. Anand Bhardwaj.
i. Why Mr. Anand Bhardwaj the then Chief 
Education Officer be not punished under 
the provisions of Contempt of Courts Act, 
1971 for his act while passing the order 
impugned in flagrant violation of the 
interim orders passed on 27.05.2020 and 
29.05.2020 in WPSS No. 507 of 2020 and 
WPSS No. 509 of 2020 and connected 
petitions?
ii. Why Mr. Anand Bhardwaj the then Chief 
Education Officer be not punished for 
giving misleading statement that there is a  clerical mistake in the order impugned?
14. Learned counsel Mrs. Neeti Rana today put 
appearance for Mr. Anand Bhardwaj the then Chief 
Education Officer and as such Mr. Anand Bhardwaj is 
directed to be impleaded as one of the respondent.
15. Learned counsel for the petitioner make 
necessary amendment by impleading Mr. Anand 
Bhardwaj as one of the respondent.
16. Let Mr. Anand Bhardwaj the then Chief 
Education Officer file his response to the charges as 
framed above.
17. Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel for the 
petitioner, apprise to this court that due to the 
pendency of all these petitions the respondents have 
withhold the consequential benefits of each of the 
petitioner.
18. In such view of the matter, the respondents are 
directed not to withhold any consequential benefits, 
which are admissible, merely on the ground that these 
petitions are pending.
19. Put up this matter on 18.02.2026 by showing the 
name of Mrs. Neeti Rana as counsel for Mr. Anand 
Bhardwaj in the cause list.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 10.01.2026
PR
